records.question: What types of content does the NOAA Technical Memorandum NMFS series published by PIFSC include?
records.ground_truth_answer: Technical workshop proceedings, large data compilations, status reports and reviews, lengthy scientific or statistical monographs, and other broad-scope scientific and technical information.
ground_truth_chunks: NMFS' Pacific Islands Fisheries Science Center (PIFSC) uses the **NOAA Technical Memorandum NMFS** series to achieve timely dissemination of scientific and technical information that is of high quality but inappropriate for publication in the formal peer-reviewed literature.
The contents are of broad scope, including technical workshop proceedings, large data compilations, status reports and reviews, lengthy scientific or statistical monographs, and more.
NOAA Technical Memoranda published by the PIFSC, although informal, are subjected to extensive review and editing and reflect sound professional work.

records.question: What are the two basic types of sediments that influence coral reefs?
records.ground_truth_answer: Terrestrially derived sediments and sediments generated in situ through erosion and the skeletal material of calcifying organisms (e.g., corals, mollusks, Halimeda, foraminifera).
ground_truth_chunks: There are two basic types of sediments that influence coral reefs: those that are terrestrially derived and those that are generated in situ through erosion and the skeletal material of calcifying organisms (corals, mollusks, *Halimeda,* foraminifera, etc.).

records.question: What mean likelihood did the BRT estimate that Mycetophyllia ferox will fall below the Critical Risk Threshold by 2100?
records.ground_truth_answer: The BRT estimated a mean likelihood of 70% (in the "likely" risk category) with a standard error of 8%.
ground_truth_chunks: The overall likelihood that *Mycetophyllia ferox* will fall below the Critical Risk Threshold by 2100 was estimated to be in the "likely" risk category with a mean likelihood of 70% and a standard error (SE) of 8% (Fig. 6.2.4).

Factors that increase the potential extinction risk (higher likelihood of falling below the Critical Risk Threshold) for *Mycetophyllia ferox* include disease, rare abundance, and observed declines in abundance.

records.question: What was the BRT's estimated mean likelihood that Pocillopora danae will fall below the Critical Risk Threshold by 2100, and what was the associated standard error and risk category?
records.ground_truth_answer: The BRT estimated a mean likelihood of 54% with a standard error (SE) of 14%, placing Pocillopora danae in the "more likely than not" risk category for falling below the Critical Risk Threshold by 2100.
ground_truth_chunks: The overall likelihood that *Pocillopora danae* will fall below the Critical Risk Threshold by 2100 was estimated to be in the "more likely than not" risk category with a mean likelihood of 54% and a standard error (SE) of 14% (Fig. 7.3.4).
This SE was calculated by taking the standard deviation of the seven mean voting scores of the BRT members and shows the coherence among the BRT.

records.question: From which geological period are fossil records of Acropora listeri reported?
ground_truth_chunks: Fossil records of *Acropora listeri* have been reported from the Pleistocene (1.8– 0.01 Ma) from Niue (Wallace, 1999).

records.question: According to Richards (2009), from where to where does Acropora verweyi's geographic range extend?
records.ground_truth_answer: It extends from east Africa, the Comorros and Seychelles in the Indian Ocean all the way to Pitcairn Island in the southeastern Pacific Ocean.
ground_truth_chunks: *Acropora verweyi* has been reported to have a relatively broad range, having the 16th largest range of 114 *Acropora* species examined (Richards, 2009), extending from east Africa, the Comorros and Seychelles in the Indian Ocean all the way to Pitcairn Island in the southeastern Pacific Ocean.

records.question: Have the reproductive characteristics of Alveopora allingi been determined?
records.ground_truth_answer: No. Reproductive characteristics of Alveopora allingi have not been determined.
ground_truth_chunks: Reproductive characteristics of *Alveopora allingi* have not been determined (Baird et al., 2009).

On temperate-latitude reefs (28o –29<sup>o</sup> S) in the Houtman Abrolhous Islands, western Australia, two colonies of *Alveopora allingi* were sampled before the main mass spawning nights in late March 1987, but there was no indication of developed gametes (Babcock et al., 1994).

records.question: Have the reproductive characteristics of Pavona bipartita been determined?
records.ground_truth_answer: No — the reproductive characteristics of Pavona bipartita have not been determined (Baird et al., 2009).
ground_truth_chunks: The reproductive characteristics of *Pavona bipartita* have not been determined (Baird et al., 2009).

However, six congeners (*Pavona cactus, Pavona chiriquiensis, Pavona clavus, Pavona duerdeni, Pavona gigantea*, and *Pavona varians*) are known to be gonochoric spawners (Baird et al., 2009); eastern Pacific populations of *Pavona varians* and the sibling agariciid species *Pavona* sp. are also known to be hermaphrodites (Glynn and Ault, 2000; Glynn et al., 2000).

records.question: What depth range has Cyphastrea ocellina been reported at?
ground_truth_chunks: **Depth range**: *Cyphastrea ocellina* has been reported in water depths ranging from 5 m to 20 m (Carpenter et al., 2008).

records.section_heading: Availability of NOAA Technical Memorandum NMFS
records.question: Where are copies of NOAA Technical Memorandum NMFS issued by the Pacific Islands Fisheries Science Center available online?
records.ground_truth_answer: On the PIFSC Web site http://www.pifsc.noaa.gov in PDF format.
ground_truth_chunks: Copies of this and other documents in the NOAA Technical Memorandum NMFS series issued by the Pacific Islands Fisheries Science Center are available online at the PIFSC Web site http://www.pifsc.noaa.gov in PDF format.

In addition, this series and a wide range of other NOAA documents are available in various formats from the National Technical Information Service, 5285 Port Royal Road, Springfield, VA 22161, U.S.A. [Tel: (703)-605- 6000]; URL: http://www.ntis.gov.
